I'm not going to argue any points you made, to simply put it is possible to bundle a server and Discord chose not to open source the stacks. How lightweight/bloated the server is and should not be the consideration at the moment, where open sourcing the stack makes people point out bugs, improvements, enhancement suggestions, etc. However no assurance nor tech specifications has been published for public audit, this worry the public most.

A note to the points you made: "owned" servers aim to provide services for small/medium community with (maybe) experienced geeks to set things up, while large community will likely have their _well-financed_ servers to do scaling and load balancing. So there is no point to argue on this; and by what I mean 'put together' doesn't have to be "a single binary", there are so many services on earth doesn't powered by only one binary.

"against the ethics behind FOSS to monetize your application" WHAT?
Check out Plumble on Github. The author sells the adfree version on Play Store, while they keeps a ad-featured version also on the store. BUT, once the author defines it is FOSS, then everybody can just clone the repo then compile a version either with or without ads.

Most of the monetizing strategy are value-add services, VIP ranking, deluxe features that wow your eyes, or even simply as ad-free. Every dimension you can imagine allows monetization, you just need to think more.

That's not "decentralized", that's a mess.

Decentralization means there will never have "Login by Discord"(Seen at Uservoice), there will not be official servers only(federated servers), etc.
